objective: Fit a simple exponential model, solve for a threshold time, and interpret a logarithm of a dimensionless ratio.
assessmentPolicy: Every sampled question is critical and must be correct without assistance. Each four-question form samples these families; it does not assess every variant or establish complete course mastery.

coverage.skill: Define the quantities and the model's operating domain
instruction: Define the quantities and the model's operating domain
examples: Interpret a supplied voltage formula with seconds and volts
Reject an exponent that mixes milliseconds with a seconds-based rate
coverage.retrieval: Name the baseline, signed deviation, reference time, rate unit and operating interval of a supplied model, then convert a millisecond input correctly.

coverage.skill: Fit a model from two positive observations
instruction: Fit a model from two positive observations
examples: Derive a growing model from two observations
Fit a fractional decay factor over a nonunit interval
coverage.retrieval: Recover a signed rate from two positive readings, verify both original observations, and explain why an exponential rate is based on a ratio.

coverage.skill: Keep the reference time separate from time zero
instruction: Keep the reference time separate from time zero
examples: Construct an anchored model when the first observation is later than zero
Recover the time-zero coefficient and verify both observations
coverage.retrieval: Rewrite an anchored fit as a time-zero model and distinguish an extrapolated coefficient from an observed reading.

coverage.skill: Check constant and incompatible observations
instruction: Check constant and incompatible observations
examples: Recognize equal positive outputs as a constant model
Distinguish contradictory same-time readings from insufficient data
Reject nonpositive data for a strictly positive exponential model
coverage.retrieval: Distinguish a zero-rate constant, repeated information, conflicting outputs and an impossible nonpositive observation.

coverage.skill: Fit deviations from a supplied baseline
instruction: Fit deviations from a supplied baseline
examples: Fit an approach to a nonzero baseline from above
Fit an increasing approach from below
Explain why an unknown baseline needs more information
coverage.retrieval: Fit signed deviations from a known baseline and give two different models demonstrating why an unknown baseline changes identifiability.

coverage.skill: Convert step factors, percentages and continuous rates
instruction: Convert step factors, percentages and continuous rates
examples: Convert a per-minute rate into a per-second rate
Contrast a signed continuous rate with a per-step percentage
coverage.retrieval: Translate between an interval percentage, its multiplication factor and a continuous rate, then change time units without changing the physical prediction.

coverage.skill: Use additional data to challenge a fit
instruction: Use additional data to challenge a fit
examples: Compute a nonzero residual at an extra observation
Distinguish interpolation from unsupported extrapolation
coverage.retrieval: Calculate a residual with its sign, classify the prediction as interpolation or extrapolation, and explain the limitation of an exact two-point fit.

coverage.skill: Understand a fit to several observations
instruction: Understand a fit to several observations
examples: Use the in-app logarithm-based fit and inspect its residual table
Explain which squared errors the fitted line minimizes
coverage.retrieval: Reconstruct the three-point logarithmic fit, calculate both kinds of residual, and explain why changing the error scale can change the fitted curve.

coverage.skill: Derive doubling time and half-life
instruction: Derive doubling time and half-life
examples: Recover a positive doubling time from a growth rate
Recover a half-life and its signed decay rate
coverage.retrieval: Derive half-life and doubling time from a dimensionless ratio and recover the signed rate from a supplied positive interval.

coverage.skill: Distinguish a time constant from a half-life
instruction: Distinguish a time constant from a half-life
examples: Evaluate the fraction remaining after one time constant
Compare the half-life and time constant of the same decay
coverage.retrieval: Explain the factor remaining after one time constant, relate it to half-life, and compare two decay rates expressed in the same units.

coverage.skill: Separate elapsed time from additional time
instruction: Separate elapsed time from additional time
examples: Recover time since the reference observation
Find additional decay time from a later measurement
coverage.retrieval: Choose the correct starting observation for a ratio, then distinguish elapsed time, additional time and the final clock reading.

coverage.skill: Solve an equality with a target
instruction: Solve an equality with a target
examples: Solve the supplied voltage threshold exactly
Keep a negative algebraic crossing separate from future operating times
coverage.retrieval: Derive an exact target time from a positive deviation ratio, substitute it, and check the original operating interval before reporting it.

coverage.skill: Solve the complete threshold inequality
instruction: Solve the complete threshold inequality
examples: Use an increasing model to select the correct side of a crossing
Use a decreasing model with strict and inclusive boundaries
Explain why an open interval has no smallest crossing time
coverage.retrieval: Use the output's direction to select the correct side of a crossing, preserve endpoint inclusion, and explain the absence of a minimum for a strict continuous interval.

coverage.skill: Check baselines and initial equality
instruction: Check baselines and initial equality
examples: Show that a decaying deviation never reaches zero in finite time
Classify a target already met at the initial time
Check an increasing approach from below
coverage.retrieval: Classify baseline targets and initial equality without taking invalid logarithms, including an increasing approach from below.

coverage.skill: Respect finite windows and constant models
instruction: Respect finite windows and constant models
examples: Clip the solution set to a closed operating interval
Handle a crossing at the last permitted time
Treat a constant model without division by zero
coverage.retrieval: Intersect exact threshold sets with finite operating windows and handle constants without dividing by zero.

coverage.skill: Find the first valid sampled observation
instruction: Find the first valid sampled observation
examples: Compare a fractional continuous crossing with two adjacent samples
Distinguish strict and inclusive conditions at an exact sample crossing
coverage.retrieval: Find a first sampled reading from an exact continuous set and check its predecessor, especially when equality lands on a sample.

coverage.skill: Build a dimensionless power ratio
instruction: Build a dimensionless power ratio
examples: Convert milliwatts and watts before taking a logarithm
Interpret a negative level as a positive power below its reference
coverage.retrieval: Convert compatible power units, form a dimensionless ratio and interpret a negative or zero referenced level correctly.

coverage.skill: Convert between a power level and a ratio
instruction: Convert between a power level and a ratio
examples: Report exact and rounded forms of a noninteger level
Recover a power from a specified level and reference
coverage.retrieval: Invert a referenced level exactly and decide whether to multiply a known reference or divide a known measured power.

coverage.skill: Keep level differences and references consistent
instruction: Keep level differences and references consistent
examples: Compare two levels with the same reference
Change the reference without changing the measured power
coverage.retrieval: Subtract levels with a shared reference, retain different references when necessary, and explain a reference change without claiming a physical power change.

coverage.skill: Separate multiplicative gains from added powers
instruction: Separate multiplicative gains from added powers
examples: Combine two specified power gain ratios
Add supplied powers before finding their total referenced level
coverage.retrieval: Choose the supplied power combination law first, then derive whether logarithmic level differences add.

coverage.skill: Derive the amplitude coefficient from a supplied relationship
instruction: Derive the amplitude coefficient from a supplied relationship
examples: Derive 20 log10 of a positive amplitude ratio from its squared power ratio
Identify the missing information in an unsupported voltage-to-power conversion
coverage.retrieval: Derive a twenty-log amplitude expression from its stated squared power-ratio relation and identify when the required premise is missing.

coverage.skill: Audit the model and the reported result
instruction: Audit the model and the reported result
examples: Reject zero and negative logarithm arguments
Check units, original substitution and a finite display near an asymptote
Explain why an exact fit alone cannot prove continued physical behavior
coverage.retrieval: Audit a threshold or referenced level for invalid premises and rounding errors, then explain why a finite fit does not prove a continuing physical law.
